root_cause.text: The function wl1271_tx_allocate() incorrectly returns -EAGAIN (interpreted by the caller as a transient buffer-full condition requiring retry) when pskb_expand_head() fails due to memory allocation failure, causing an infinite retry loop and CPU soft lockup in wlcore_tx_work_locked().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the return value from -EAGAIN to -ENOMEM in wl1271_tx_allocate() when pskb_expand_head() fails. The CVE description explains that -EAGAIN is misinterpreted as aggregation buffer full, leading to flushing, re-queuing, and immediate retry with GFP_ATOMIC, which results in an infinite loop under mutex.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect error code: return -ENOMEM instead of -EAGAIN when pskb_expand_head fails due to memory exhaustion.
intent_record.what: Changed the return value from -EAGAIN to -ENOMEM when pskb_expand_head fails in the wl1271_tx_allocate function.
intent_record.how: The call to pskb_expand_head can fail due to memory allocation failure. Previously, the function returned -EAGAIN, which suggests the caller should retry the operation. Returning -ENOMEM now correctly indicates an out-of-memory condition, which is not transient, changing the caller's error handling behavior.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement incorrectly returns -EAGAIN when pskb_expand_head() fails due to memory exhaustion. The caller interprets -EAGAIN as a transient buffer-full condition and retries indefinitely, causing an infinite loop and CPU soft lockup in wlcore_tx_work_locked().
